note: Reader-facing release notes for returning readers (modules/reading-switches.mjs). Newest first. Plain words, no internals.

notes: X-ray reading, in Switches: hover a word, a sentence or a paragraph and the structure shows through — the threads a word belongs to, the way a sentence leans, the sign a paragraph sits under. Click to hold it.
The ants have noticed the egg.
A folio wall: pages under glass, the maker's first. New folios stay liquid until a stone day passes, then go clear.
The ants under the berry rows have torches now, and streets; the Genie, it turns out, did good business with them.
Boof works for the land, not for fruit — a slip that had lingered in the copy is mended everywhere it stood.
Page controls are quieter, and on a phone the page runs to the edge. The genre dial folds away until you want it.
The chapters read in shorter beats now: the long walls of text are broken where the story turns, and the longest sentences breathe.
Genre is tunable: under any chapter's title, choose Tune and move the point between fairy tale, absurd reality and low magic. The story follows the blend.
Every chapter now opens with a choice: read it as Boon, Bane or Bone — the fairytale, the reality being left behind, or the notation underneath.
Several chapters were revised to follow the Egg more closely: less bookkeeping, more warmth, more of what can't be named yet.
The last chapter has a new name: The Shell-Shaped Door.
The margins have started to notice something. Keep an eye on them.
The Scriptorium is now your desk: pick up where you left off, search every chapter, keep the book offline, and see when the next chapter lands.
Everything on the desk is a spell you can tap, then type. Press / there and try ?[next].
The four design lenses in the Scriptorium are now named for the forces they exert: inertia, friction, flux, resonance.
Every chapter now ends with its shelf-mates in any library: call numbers to take into the aisles, and a way to find them near you.
A new trial for readers who keep coming back: the grammar, faintly — each part of a chapter shows the sign it enacts.
Lore.Land can live on your home screen now, and keep every chapter for reading offline (see Switches).
When the network is gone, the offline page shows the chapters on your shelf.
Sharing a chapter shows its painting and title.
Chapter One's opening was tightened: the warm furrow arrives sooner.
A reading nook in the rail: coziness, texture, light from daylight to lamplight, and an optional hearth.
Each chapter now ends by turning the page toward the next one, and the contents are one tap from the dock.
Select any line to get a link straight to it.
Nothing you used went away: the rail and summary are as you left them. See Switches in the rail.
